messages.subject: casting factors ?
parts:
Hi everybody

I have a stubborn problem that I expected to be easy but it isn't.

I have a molten data frame with a person.id, a variable and a value column. I want to cast it to a data frame so that i have only 1 row for each person and have as many columns as there are unique variables and have the values for each variable / persons combination in in the person row and variable column

This generates as toy example of what I have:

df = data.frame(pers.id = rep(1:4,each = 5), variable = paste("Var", rep(LETTERS[1:5], 4), sep=""))
df[which(df$variable!="VarE"),"value"] <- sample(c("Yes","No"),16, replace=T)
df[which(df$variable=="VarE"),"value"] <- sample(c("1","0"),4, replace=T)
df$value <- as.factor(df$value)
> head(df,8)
pers.id variable value
1 1 VarA No
2 1 VarB Yes
3 1 VarC Yes
4 1 VarD No
5 1 VarE 1
6 2 VarA No
7 2 VarB Yes
8 2 VarC Yes
This is what i need at the end.

required <- data.frame(pers.id = 1:4,
VarA = as.factor(as.character(df[which(df$variable=="VarA"), "value"])),
VarB = as.factor(as.character(df[which(df$variable=="VarB"), "value"])),
VarC = as.factor(as.character(df[which(df$variable=="VarC"), "value"])),
VarD = as.factor(as.character(df[which(df$variable=="VarD"), "value"])),
VarE = as.integer(as.character(df[which(df$variable=="VarE"), "value"]))
)
> required
pers.id VarA VarB VarC VarD VarE
1 1 No Yes Yes No 1
2 2 No Yes Yes Yes 1
3 3 No Yes Yes No 1
4 4 Yes Yes Yes Yes 0
> str(required)
'data.frame': 4 obs. of 6 variables:
$ pers.id: int 1 2 3 4
$ VarA : Factor w/ 2 levels "No","Yes": 1 1 1 2
$ VarB : Factor w/ 1 level "Yes": 1 1 1 1
$ VarC : Factor w/ 1 level "Yes": 1 1 1 1
$ VarD : Factor w/ 2 levels "No","Yes": 1 2 1 2
$ VarE : int 1 1 1 0

My real life problem have hundreds of columns and they change every day.

I suspect one can solve this with cast() because the input dataframe is the result of melt() but I have not found a way to do it. I imagine the result of the correct cast would have only one additional column with the length of each combination of person and variable (which would be 1 if all goes well).

Is cast() the appropriate tool for this or should I use something else

thanks in advance

Christiaan Pauw

messages.subject: Re: casting factors ?
parts:
Hi Christiaan,

You never say what the problem is exactly. What have you tried? What
went wrong? In any case, it seems like you just need

cast(df, pers.id ~ variable)

or using the newer reshape2 package:

dcast(df, pers.id ~ variable)


Or am I missing something?

Best,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: casting factors ?
parts:
Thanks Ista

Your code works on the examples but for some reason not on my real life data although as far as I can see the essential structure is the same (see output of str() below the text).

My problems are: (my dataframe is called 'mpers')

1.When in try you suggestion on my real data with cast(mpers, pers.id ~ variable) it takes very long. It never actually finishes - I have to stop it

2. When in use dcast I loose the category labels. It works faster with dcast(mpers, pers.id ~ variable) but all the columns are integers - even where factors were expected . Interesting also that if i run the example with your code I don't get a warning, but for my real life code I get "Aggregation function missing: defaulting to length".

I found that if I manually split - apply - combine I can get the desired result:

persons <- split(df, f = df$pers.id)
persons <- lapply(persons, na.omit)
persons <- persons[sapply(persons, function(x) all(is.na(x))==FALSE)]
persons <- lapply(persons, FUN=function(x) dcast(x, pers.id ~ variable))
dd <- rbind.fill(persons)
dd == required

What puzzles me is 'dcast(df, pers.id ~ variable)' works straight away with the example data as you have demonstrated but not with my real life data. I have checked the structure and tehr are no missing values in the 'value' column.

I would still be interested to understand this issue even though there is a workaround

Thanks again to Ista and everybody on this great list
best regards
Christiaan
